name: Flowbase
tagline: Project management that thinks like your team does.
target_audience: Distributed teams of 10-50 at Series A/B startups who outgrew spreadsheets
key_differentiator: AI-generated weekly status summaries pulled automatically from task activity, no manual reporting
weaknesses: Weak native time tracking; integrations limited to 15 apps versus competitors' 100+; mobile app frequently lags behind desktop feature releases

name: Trellix Pro
target_audience: Small creative and marketing teams (5-20 people) who think in boards, not tables
key_differentiator: Deepest kanban customization on the market, including swimlanes, WIP limits, and per-card automation recipes
weaknesses: No native Gantt or timeline view; reporting is basic CSV export only; struggles past ~30 concurrent boards per workspace

name: Orbitwork
tagline: Enterprise delivery, without the enterprise drag.
target_audience: IT and ops teams at 500+ employee companies managing cross-departmental programs
key_differentiator: Resource capacity planning across departments with real-time overallocation warnings, built for PMO-level oversight
weaknesses: Steep learning curve, typical onboarding takes 4-6 weeks; requires a dedicated admin; no usable free tier

name: Nudge
tagline: The to-do list that manages itself.
target_audience: Solo founders and freelancers juggling multiple client projects alone
key_differentiator: Auto-prioritizes your daily task list using deadline proximity and client-value tags you set once
price_tier: free tier + low paid ($5/mo for unlimited projects)
weaknesses: No team collaboration features at all; single-user by design; cannot assign tasks to others even on paid tier

name: Ridgeline
tagline: Built for teams who ship on a schedule.
target_audience: Engineering and product teams running sprint-based delivery at 20-200 person companies
key_differentiator: Native two-way sync with Git commits and pull requests, so task status updates itself from code activity
weaknesses: Overkill and confusing for non-technical teams; sprint/velocity features are unused dead weight for anyone outside engineering; support is community-forum only below the top pricing tier
